help.title: Probability Plot
help.body:
Description
A probability plot (as in Minitab) shows the values of a variable on the X axis and the corresponding cumulative percentages on the Y axis. The Y axis is scaled so that, if the data follow the selected distribution, the points fall approximately on a straight line. The plot is used to assess how well a distribution fits the data and to estimate percentiles. This is different from a P-P plot (probabilities on both axes) and from a Q-Q plot (theoretical quantiles on the X axis).
Options
  • Variable(s): one or more numeric variables. By default a separate plot is drawn for every variable. Check "Overlay multiple variables in a single plot" to draw them in one plot.
  • Group by: an optional category variable. Each level is fitted separately and shown in a different color and shape.
  • Distribution: Normal, Lognormal, Weibull, Exponential, Logistic, Loglogistic, Smallest extreme value, Largest extreme value.
  • Parameter estimation method: Maximum likelihood or Least squares (regression of the data values on the plotting positions).
  • Plotting position: Median rank (Benard) (i-0.3)/(n+0.4), Mean rank i/(n+1), or Hazen (i-0.5)/n.
  • Y-axis scale type: Percent, Probability or Score (the transformed value used by the chosen distribution, e.g. the z-score for the normal distribution).
  • Show confidence interval: draws approximate pointwise confidence limits (two-sided, lower or upper) around the fitted line at the confidence level that you specify.
  • Facets: draws a separate panel for each level of the selected variable(s). Each panel is fitted separately.
Output
The fitted line, the plotted points and (optionally) confidence limits are drawn on the plot. The estimated distribution parameters, N, the Anderson-Darling statistic (AD) and its p-value can be shown on the plot and as an output table. The p-value for Normal and Lognormal (Maximum likelihood) comes from the Anderson-Darling test in the nortest package. For all other cases (other distributions, or Least squares) the p-value is a parametric bootstrap p-value: samples are simulated from the fitted distribution, refitted with the same method, and the p-value is the share of simulated AD statistics that are at least as large as the observed one. The number of iterations is set in Options (default 600, 0 = do not compute, in which case the p-value shows as NA). A fixed random seed (123) is used so results are reproducible. A footer under the output table states how the p-values were obtained.
Package
ggplot2;ggthemes;nortest;
